title: House Robber
statement: Given an integer array nums representing the amount of money of each house along a street, return the maximum amount of money you can rob tonight without alerting the police (cannot rob two adjacent houses).
hints: At house i, you have two choices: rob house i (add nums[i] + dp[i-2]) or skip it (keep dp[i-1]).

solutions.title: 1D DP Table
Two Variable Rolling DP

editorial.approach: At each house i, you either rob house i (adding its value to the maximum looted up to house i-2) or skip house i (keeping the maximum looted up to house i-1). This yields recurrence dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]). Maintain two rolling variables representing prev1 (best up to previous house) and prev2 (best up to house before that).
editorial.why_optimal: Runs in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space, compressing the 1D DP table into two scalar variables without auxiliary array allocation.
editorial.pitfalls: Edge cases with empty arrays or single-element arrays returning incorrect indices. Forgetting to update the rolling state variables in atomic sequence.
